# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Conventions

- Controllers live in `Controllers/`, one per resource, route `api/[controller]`. Request bodies are `record` types declared inside the controller.
- Controllers inherit `ApiControllerBase` and use `Handle(...)` so service errors map to 404, 409 and 400.
- Every endpoint is behind sign-in. Restrict actions with `[RequireRole("...")]`: destructive actions are Admin only, approvals are Approver or Admin.
- Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
- Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
- Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
- Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
- End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.

## Commands

- Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
- Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`

## Demo accounts (not real credentials)

- `[REDACTED]` / `[REDACTED]` (role Approver)
- `[REDACTED]` / `[REDACTED]` (role Admin)

## Never

- Commit real credentials, tokens or customer data.
- Add business logic to `Program.cs` or controllers.

# [Custom Agents (.agent.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-agents)

Custom personas with specific tools, instructions, and behaviors. Use for orchestrated workflows with role-based tool restrictions.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/agents/*.agent.md` | Workspace |
| `<profile>/agents/*.agent.md` | User profile |

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
description: "<required>"    # For agent picker and subagent discovery
name: "Agent Name"           # Optional, defaults to filename
tools: [search, web]         # Optional: aliases, MCP (<server>/*), extension tools
model: "Claude Sonnet 4"     # Optional, uses picker default; supports array for fallback
reasoning-effort: "high"     # Optional: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
argument-hint: "Task..."     # Optional, input guidance
agents: [agent1, agent2]     # Optional, restrict allowed subagents by name (omit = all, [] = none)
user-invocable: true         # Optional, show in agent picker (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false  # Optional, prevent subagent invocation (default: false)
handoffs: [...]              # Optional, transitions to other agents
hooks:                       # Optional, inline hooks for this agent's lifecycle events
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/validate.sh"
  PostToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/format.sh"
---
```

### Invocation Control

| Attribute | Default | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `user-invocable: false` | `true` | Hide from agent picker, only accessible as subagent |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | `false` | Prevent other agents from invoking as subagent |

### Model Fallback

```yaml
model: ['Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)', 'GPT-5 (copilot)']  # First available model is used
```

### Reasoning Effort

Use `reasoning-effort` to set the reasoning level for the custom agent's model:

```yaml
reasoning-effort: high  # low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
```

The selected model must support the configured level. If omitted, the runtime resolves the effort from the model configuration and, when applicable, the parent agent.

## Tools

Sources: built-in aliases, specific tools, MCP servers (`<server>/*`), extension tools.

**Special**: `[]` = no tools, omit = defaults. Body reference: `#tool:<name>`

### Tool Aliases

| Alias | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `execute` | Run shell commands |
| `read` | Read file contents |
| `edit` | Edit files |
| `search` | Search files or text |
| `agent` | Invoke custom agents as subagents |
| `web` | Fetch URLs and web search |
| `todo` | Manage task lists |

### Common Patterns

```yaml
tools: [read, search]             # Read-only research
tools: [myserver/*]               # MCP server only
tools: [read, edit, search]       # No terminal access
tools: []                         # Conversational only
```

To discover available tools, check your current tool list or use `#tool:` syntax in the body to reference specific tools.

## Template

```markdown
---
description: "{Use when... trigger phrases for subagent discovery}"
tools: [{minimal set of tool aliases}]
user-invocable: false
---
You are a specialist at {specific task}. Your job is to {clear purpose}.

## Constraints
- DO NOT {thing this agent should never do}
- DO NOT {another restriction}
- ONLY {the one thing this agent does}

## Approach
1. {Step one of how this agent works}
2. {Step two}
3. {Step three}

## Output Format
{Exactly what this agent should return}
```

## Invocation

- **Manual**: Agent selector in chat
- **Subagent**: Parent agent delegates based on `description` match (when `infer` allows)

## Core Principles

1. **Single role**: One persona with focused responsibilities per agent
2. **Minimal tools**: Only include what the role needs—excess tools dilute focus
3. **Clear boundaries**: Define what the agent should NOT do
4. **Keyword-rich description**: Include trigger words so parent agents know when to delegate

## Anti-patterns

- **Swiss-army agents**: Too many tools, tries to do everything
- **Vague descriptions**: "A helpful agent" doesn't guide delegation—be specific
- **Role confusion**: Description doesn't match body persona
- **Circular handoffs**: A → B → A without progress criteria

## Inline Hooks

Custom agents support inline `hooks` in frontmatter. These hooks execute shell commands at agent lifecycle points and are scoped to this agent only. The format matches standalone hook files (see [hooks reference](../hooks.md)).

### Supported Events

`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `Stop`

### Example

```yaml
---
description: "Secure code reviewer that blocks dangerous commands"
tools: [read, search, execute]
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/block-dangerous-cmds.sh"
      timeout: 10
  PostToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/auto-lint.sh"
---
```

Each hook command supports: `type` (must be `command`), `command`, platform overrides (`windows`, `linux`, `osx`), `cwd`, `env`, `timeout`.

# [Agent Skills (SKILL.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/agent-skills)

Folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents load on-demand for specialized tasks.

## Structure

```
.github/skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md           # Required (name must match folder)
├── scripts/           # Executable code
├── references/        # Docs loaded as needed
└── assets/            # Templates, boilerplate
```

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `~/.copilot/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` | Personal |

## SKILL.md Format

```yaml
---
name: skill-name              # Required: 1-64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, must match folder
description: 'What and when to use. Max 1024 chars.'
argument-hint: 'Optional hint shown for slash invocation'
user-invocable: true          # Optional: show as slash command (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false # Optional: disable automatic model-triggered loading
---
```

### Body

- What the skill accomplishes
- When to use (triggers and use cases)
- Step-by-step procedures
- References to resources: `[script](./scripts/test.js)`

## Template

```markdown
---
name: webapp-testing
description: 'Test web applications using Playwright. Use for verifying frontend, debugging UI, capturing screenshots.'
---

# Web Application Testing

## When to Use
- Verify frontend functionality
- Debug UI behavior

## Procedure
1. Start the web server
2. Run [test script](./scripts/test.js)
3. Review screenshots in `./screenshots/`
```

## Progressive Loading

1. **Discovery** (~100 tokens): Agent reads `name` and `description`
2. **Instructions** (<5000 tokens): Loads `SKILL.md` body when relevant
3. **Resources**: Additional files load only when referenced

Keep file references one level deep from `SKILL.md`.

## Slash Command Behavior

Skills and prompt files both appear after typing `/` in chat.

| Configuration | Slash command | Auto-loaded |
|---|---|---|
| Default (both omitted) | Yes | Yes |
| `user-invocable: false` | No | Yes |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | Yes | No |
| Both set | No | No |

## When to Use

Repeatable, on-demand workflows with bundled assets (scripts, templates, reference docs).

## Core Principles

1. **Keyword-rich descriptions**: Include trigger words for discovery
2. **Progressive loading**: Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines; use reference files
3. **Relative paths**: Always use `./` for skill resources
4. **Self-contained**: Include all procedural knowledge to complete the task

## Anti-patterns

- **Vague descriptions**: "A helpful skill" doesn't enable discovery
- **Monolithic SKILL.md**: Everything in one file instead of references
- **Name mismatch**: Folder name doesn't match `name` field
- **Missing procedures**: Descriptions without step-by-step guidance

# [agent instructions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-instructions)

Guidelines that automatically apply to all chat requests across your entire workspace.

## File Types (Choose One)

| File | Location | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `copilot-instructions.md` | `.github/` | Project-wide standards (recommended, cross-editor) |
| `AGENTS.md` | Root or subfolders | Open standard, monorepo hierarchy support |

Use **only one**—not both.

## Template

Only include sections the workspace benefits from:

```markdown
# Project Guidelines

## Code Style
{Language and formatting preferences—reference key files that exemplify patterns}

## Architecture
{Major components, service boundaries, the "why" behind structural decisions}

## Build and Test
{Commands to install, build, test—agents will attempt to run these}

## Conventions
{Patterns that differ from common practices—include specific examples}
```

For large repos, link to detailed docs instead of embedding: `See docs/TESTING.md for test conventions.`

## When to Use

- General coding standards that apply everywhere
- Team preferences shared through version control
- Project-wide requirements (testing, documentation)

## Core Principles

1. **Minimal by default**: Only what's relevant to *every* task
2. **Concise and actionable**: Every line should guide behavior
3. **Link, don't embed**: Reference docs instead of copying content. Search for existing docs (`docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, etc.) and catalog what they cover—only inline agent-critical gotchas not documented elsewhere
4. **Keep current**: Update when practices change

## Anti-patterns

- **Using both file types**: Having both `copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`
- **Kitchen sink**: Everything instead of what matters most
- **Duplicating docs**: Copying README instead of linking
- **Obvious instructions**: Conventions already enforced by linters

# Invoice Approval Demo App

A small invoice approval app used for live AI-in-SDLC demos. It is deliberately simple: a .NET 8 API, a plain web UI, and an in-memory store, so it runs with one command and no database.

## Run it

```
dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api
```

Open http://localhost:5000 and sign in:

| User | Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[REDACTED]` | `[REDACTED]` | Approver |
| `[REDACTED]` | `[REDACTED]` | Admin |

These are demo accounts for a local, in-memory app. They are not real credentials.

## What it does

1. Create an invoice (it starts as a draft).
2. Submit it for approval.
3. An approver approves it, or rejects it with a reason.

Invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, then Approved or Rejected.

## Tests

```
dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln
```

## AI interaction logging

Repository-local Copilot hooks in `.github/hooks/` append lifecycle events to
`logs/ai-interactions.jsonl`. Start a new VS Code Copilot session in this
repository to enable them. The hooks record prompts, tool calls and outcomes,
session identifiers, available agent/subagent metadata, and model metadata only
when the runtime supplies it. Missing metadata is omitted.

The logger does not read or record process environment variables. It also
redacts common [REDACTED] and secret-like values in recorded text. Prompt
and tool data can still contain sensitive information, so treat the local log
as private and review it before sharing. The generated JSONL file is
gitignored.

`PreToolUse` is a Copilot command hook; if Python is unavailable or the log
cannot be written, Copilot may deny that tool call. Keep Python 3 available
and ensure the repository log directory is writable.

Verify the hook logger without changing the repository log:

```
python3 .github/hooks/verify_ai_interaction_logging.py
```

## Project layout

```
backend/
  src/InvoiceApp.Domain   business rules
  src/InvoiceApp.Api      controllers, sign-in, web UI (wwwroot)
  tests/InvoiceApp.Tests  xUnit tests
docs/use-cases            short feature briefs
AGENTS.md                 conventions for AI coding agents
```

## Use cases

- [UC-1 Bulk invoice approval](docs/use-cases/UC-1-bulk-approval.md)
- [UC-2 Partial approval](docs/use-cases/UC-2-partial-approval.md)
File too large to read at once (28.1 KB). Consider using the grep tool to search within the file, or view with view_range to read specific sections.

# [Hooks (.json)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/hooks)

Deterministic lifecycle automation for agent sessions. Use hooks to enforce policy, automate validation, and inject runtime context.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/hooks/*.json` | Workspace (team-shared) |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Workspace local (not committed) |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Workspace |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | User profile |

Hooks from all configured locations are collected and executed; workspace and user hooks do not override each other.

## Hook Events

| Event | Trigger |
|------|-------|
| `SessionStart` | First prompt of a new agent session |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits a prompt |
| `PreToolUse` | Before tool invocation |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool invocation |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compaction |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent starts |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent ends |
| `Stop` | Agent session ends |

## Configuration Format

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "./scripts/validate-tool.sh",
        "timeout": 15
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each hook command supports:
- `type` (must be `command`)
- `command` (default)
- `windows`, `linux`, `osx` (platform overrides)
- `cwd`, `env`, `timeout`

## Input / Output Contract

Hooks receive JSON on stdin and can return JSON on stdout.

- Common output: `continue`, `stopReason`, `systemMessage`
- `PreToolUse` permissions are read from `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (`allow` | `ask` | `deny`)
- `PostToolUse` output can block further processing with `decision: block`

`PreToolUse` example output:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "ask",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Needs user confirmation"
  }
}
```

Exit codes:
- `0` success
- `2` blocking error
- Other values produce non-blocking warnings

## Hooks vs Other Customizations

| Primitive | Behavior |
|------|-------|
| Instructions / Prompts / Skills / Agents | Guidance (non-deterministic) |
| Hooks | Runtime enforcement and deterministic automation |

Use hooks when behavior must be guaranteed (for example: block dangerous commands, force validation, auto-inject context).

## Core Principles

1. Keep hooks small and auditable
2. Validate and sanitize hook inputs
3. Avoid hardcoded secrets in scripts
4. Prefer workspace hooks for team policy, user hooks for personal automation

## Anti-patterns

- Running long hooks that block normal flow
- Using hooks where plain instructions are sufficient
- Letting agents edit hook scripts without approval controls

# UC-1: Bulk invoice approval

## Background

Finance operations approvers open every pending invoice one at a time. For a school district with 40 invoices in a batch, that is 40 separate approvals.

## The idea

Approvers should be able to select several pending invoices and approve them together.

## What the business asked for

- Select multiple pending invoices from one screen.
- See a summary before confirming: number of invoices, total amount, customers involved.
- Exclude individual invoices from the batch before confirming.
- Keep an audit trail: who approved what, and when, for every invoice in the batch.
- Invoices over $1,000 need a second approver before they are final.

## Out of scope for the first release

- Email notifications (in-app only for now).

## Open questions (good prompts for clarifying questions)

- What happens to the rest of the batch if one invoice fails?
- Can the same person be both approvers on a large invoice?
- Is there a limit on batch size?

# UC-2: Partial approval


## Background

Today an invoice is approved or rejected as a whole. Two school districts asked for a way to approve less than the full amount when part of an invoice is disputed.

## The change

An approver can approve an invoice for an amount lower than the invoiced amount, with a required note explaining why.

## What the business asked for

- The approver enters the approved amount, which must be greater than zero and less than the invoiced amount.
- Both the invoiced amount and the approved amount are kept on the invoice.
- The invoice shows as partially approved, separate from fully approved.
- A note is required whenever the approved amount is lower than the invoiced amount.
- Existing approve and reject behaviour stays exactly as it is.

## Where it touches the code

The existing approval flow: `ApprovalService`, `ApprovalsController`, and the Approvals tab in the web UI.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Conventions

- Controllers live in `Controllers/`, one per resource, route `api/[controller]`. Request bodies are `record` types declared inside the controller.
- Controllers inherit `ApiControllerBase` and use `Handle(...)` so service errors map to 404, 409 and 400.
- Every endpoint is behind sign-in. Restrict actions with `[RequireRole("...")]`: destructive actions are Admin only, approvals are Approver or Admin.
- Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
- Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
- Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
- Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
- End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.

## Commands

- Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
- Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`

## Approval policy for future changes

These are assignment requirements for future approval work; they are not implemented by the current single-approver flow. Keep business rules in `ApprovalService` and add tests before changing behavior.

- A Manager's approval limit is 50,000.
- A Director's approval limit is 500,000.
- An invoice above 500,000 requires two distinct approvers, and the second approval must be by a Director.
- Rejection must not alter the submitted invoice data (for example, its amount or customer). Record the rejection outcome and its decision metadata without rewriting that data. If “without mutation” is intended to prohibit even outcome/decision metadata writes, get human clarification before implementation.

# UC-2: Partial approval


## Background

Today an invoice is approved or rejected as a whole. Two school districts asked for a way to approve less than the full amount when part of an invoice is disputed.

## The change

An approver can approve an invoice for an amount lower than the invoiced amount, with a required note explaining why.

## What the business asked for

- The approver enters the approved amount, which must be greater than zero and less than the invoiced amount.
- Both the invoiced amount and the approved amount are kept on the invoice.
- The invoice shows as partially approved, separate from fully approved.
- A note is required whenever the approved amount is lower than the invoiced amount.
- Existing approve and reject behaviour stays exactly as it is.

The existing approval flow: `ApprovalService`, `ApprovalsController`, and the Approvals tab in the web UI.

---
name: implementation-agent
description: "Use when implementing an explicitly approved invoice-approval feature or bug fix in the API, domain, or UI."
tools: [read, search, edit, execute, agent]
agents: [test-agent, review-agent]
user-invocable: true
---

You implement approved changes in this invoice approval application. Follow the repository's `AGENTS.md`; keep business rules in the Domain project and preserve existing authentication and logging behavior.

## Workflow

1. Read the relevant code, tests, and `invoice-approval-rules` skill before changing approval behavior.
2. Check for unresolved policy decisions in `AGENTS.md`. If a requested change depends on one, stop and ask the human owner rather than choosing an interpretation.
3. Make the smallest complete implementation and add/update tests only as part of an explicitly requested feature task.
4. Delegate focused test design and execution to `test-agent`, then request an independent read-only review from `review-agent`. Do not delegate unresolved product decisions.
5. Address reported defects, run the relevant repository checks, and report files changed, results, and any remaining decisions.

## Boundaries

- Do not change authentication, demo roles, or approval thresholds without explicit human direction.
- Do not modify `.github/hooks/` or the interaction logger unless explicitly requested.
- Do not claim a policy is implemented merely because it is documented.

---
name: test-agent
description: "Use when designing, adding, or running focused unit, integration, or Playwright tests for invoice-approval behavior."
tools: [read, search, edit, execute, agent]
agents: [review-agent]
user-invocable: true
---

You own test design and test execution for this invoice approval application. Use the `test-quality` and, for approval rules, `invoice-approval-rules` skills. Follow the test conventions in `AGENTS.md`.

## Workflow

1. Identify the behavior that has been explicitly specified and distinguish it from unresolved decisions.
2. Add or adjust focused tests only when the task requests test changes; otherwise run the relevant existing tests without editing them.
3. Cover meaningful boundaries, invalid transitions, persistence effects, and role/identity distinctions where the policy is settled.
4. Do not encode assumptions about unresolved first-approver eligibility, threshold inclusivity, or mapping Manager/Director to `Approver`/`Admin`. Ask the human owner or report the blocked coverage.
5. After test changes, delegate a read-only test-focused review to `review-agent`; report exact commands, outcomes, and gaps.

## Boundaries

- Do not alter production behavior, authentication, demo roles, or logging hooks.
- Do not weaken or delete a failing test merely to make the suite pass.
- Do not represent unrun tests as passing.

---
name: review-agent
description: "Use for an independent, read-only review of invoice approval implementation or tests for correctness, policy compliance, and regressions."
tools: [read, search]
agents: []
user-invocable: true
---

You provide an independent, read-only review of proposed or completed changes to this invoice approval application. Use `invoice-approval-rules` and `test-quality` when relevant, and compare the change with `AGENTS.md` and the actual diff.

## Review approach

1. Check correctness, lifecycle and persistence effects, [REDACTED], test coverage, and regressions.
2. Treat unresolved policy questions as blockers; do not infer first-approver eligibility or map business roles to demo roles.
3. Do not edit files, run commands, or delegate. Return findings first, ordered by severity, with file and line references; distinguish confirmed defects from open decisions.
4. If there are no findings, state that explicitly and note any limits of the review.

Send findings back to the requesting human or orchestrating agent for resolution; do not make fixes yourself.

## Quick Start

[](#quick-start)

Install OpenSpec. On macOS or Linux, in your terminal:

curl -fsSL https://openspec.dev/cli/install.sh | sh

On Windows, in PowerShell:

irm https://openspec.dev/cli/install.ps1 | iex

Prefer a package manager? `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest` (needs Node.js 22.12.0 or higher) or the official [Homebrew formula](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openspec), `brew install openspec`.

Then navigate to your project directory and initialize:

cd your-project
openspec init

> **Want your AI to do it?** Paste the [setup prompt](https://openspec.dev/docs/installation#install-with-your-ai-assistant) into your coding assistant — it installs the CLI, runs `openspec init`, and verifies the result.

Now talk to your AI:

*   **Not sure what to build yet?** Start with `/opsx:explore`, a no-stakes thinking partner that reads your code, weighs options, and shapes a plan before any code gets written. ([Quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart))
*   **Already know what you want?** Go straight to `/opsx:propose <what-you-want-to-build>`.

Both are in the default profile. If you want the expanded workflow (`/opsx:new`, `/opsx:continue`, `/opsx:ff`, `/opsx:verify`, `/opsx:bulk-archive`, `/opsx:onboard`), select it with `openspec config profile` and apply with `openspec update`.

`/opsx:propose` is the canonical name; your tool may spell it `/opsx-propose` (Cursor, GitHub Copilot), `@opsx-propose` (Amazon Q) or `$openspec-propose` (Codex). `openspec init` prints the right form for the tools you picked — see [Supported Tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).

Contents of https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart: Your first change, from idea to archived, in a new or existing project. Before you start, you need the CLI on your machine ([Installation](/docs/installation)) and OpenSpec initialized in your project ([Set up your project](/docs/setup)). ## [Start from an empty project](#start-from-an-empty-project) You can start without a chosen stack or a complete architecture. Initialize OpenSpec in your project folder, then ask your agent to explore the options with you. In your AI chat: ``` Help me explore a task tracker from scratch. I have not picked a stack. Compare the options and help me choose the first behavior to build. ``` Decide what the first change needs and leave later architecture choices open. Ask your agent to propose that one change, then follow the steps below. You can revisit the architecture as the project grows. ## [The loop at a glance](#the-loop-at-a-glance) Every change moves through the same five steps: you think the idea through with your agent, it drafts a plan, you correct the plan before any code exists, the agent builds from it, and archiving updates your specs with what shipped. Mermaid diagram source: flowchart LR explore\["1 · Explore\
think it through together"\] --> propose\["2 · Propose\
agent drafts the plan"\] propose --> review\["3 · Review\
you correct the plan"\] review --> apply\["4 · Apply\
agent builds, task by task"\] apply --> archive\["5 · Archive\
specs absorb the change"\] archive -. "next change" .-> explore Every prompt below goes in your AI chat, the same place you ask for code. The examples use plain language so they work across tools. You can also invoke a skill directly; the syntax varies by tool ([supported tools](/docs/supported-tools)). ## [Step 1: Explore](#step-1-explore) Think the idea through with your agent before you ask for a plan. In your AI chat: ``` Help me explore how rate limiting should work in this app. ``` Explore is a thinking mode. The agent investigates your codebase, asks the questions that matter, sketches options, and challenges assumptions. It never writes code. It writes nothing else unless you ask it to capture what you decided, or say yes when it offers. The output is a sharper idea. Stay here as long as the problem needs. When the shape feels right, hand it off: ``` Propose the change we just discussed. ``` That line starts propose for you, carrying everything you settled. Skip the first prompt in step 2. ## [Step 2: Propose](#step-2-propose) Propose turns the idea into a reviewable plan. Coming from explore, it's already running. Starting cold, when the change is clear in your head, ask directly. In your AI chat: ``` Propose a change to add rate limiting. ``` The agent asks what it needs to, then writes a change folder: ``` openspec/changes/add-rate-limiting/ ├── proposal.md why, and what changes ├── specs/ what "done" means, as testable requirements ├── design.md technical decisions (only when the change needs one) └── tasks.md the implementation checklist ``` No code yet. Propose stops at the plan. ## [Step 3: Review and correct the plan](#step-3-review-and-correct-the-plan) Fix the plan while it's still words and nothing is built yet. Read in this order: * **`proposal.md`**: is this the right problem, at the right size? * **`specs/`**: the highest-value read. Would you accept these requirements as done? * **`tasks.md`**: do the tasks cover the specs, and nothing more? To fix something, either works: * Edit the file yourself. The artifacts are plain markdown, and the files are the plan. * Tell your agent what's wrong ("the spec is missing the unauthenticated case"). It revises the artifacts. ## [Step 4: Apply](#step-4-apply) Apply turns the plan into code. Start a fresh chat session, since implementation goes better on a clean context window. In your AI chat: ``` Apply the add-rate-limiting change. ``` The agent reads the change folder, then works through `tasks.md`, checking off each task as it lands. * **Interrupted, or out of context?** Open a new session and ask it to apply again. It resumes at the first unchecked task. * **Plan turned out wrong?** Fix the artifacts (either way from step 3), then continue applying. * **Progress** lives in the `tasks.md` checkboxes. There is no hidden state. ## [Step 5: Archive](#step-5-archive) Archiving does two things: it updates your main specs with the change's requirements, and it moves the change folder into the archive folder (in `/openspec/changes/archive/*`). When every box in `tasks.md` is checked, in your AI chat: ``` Archive the add-rate-limiting change. ``` Step through what archiving does: Step 1The finished change Implementation is done. The delta spec (what this change adds) still sits inside the change folder; specs/ doesn't know about rate limiting yet. openspec/ ├── specs/ (no rate-limiting spec yet) └── changes/ └── add-rate-limiting/ ├── proposal.md ├── tasks.md every box checked └── specs/ └── rate-limiting/ └── spec.md the delta: ADDED requirements Git is a separate concern. Commit the change folder with the code, and nothing else about your workflow changes. ### [Keep or prune archived changes](#keep-or-prune-archived-changes) `openspec/changes/archive/` keeps the proposal, design, tasks, and delta for each finished change. In the archive flow above, the delta has already updated `openspec/specs/`. * **Keep the whole change folder** when you want a self-contained record in the current checkout. * **Remove an archived change's `specs/` folder** when Git is your spec history. Commit the archive first, then delete `openspec/changes/archive//specs/`. The proposal, design, and tasks remain in the checkout. `openspec validate --archived` still works because it checks task completion, not applied deltas. * **Remove the whole change folder** only when you no longer need its proposal, design, or task history in the checkout. The current specs do not change, but `openspec validate --archived` and searches of the checkout no longer include that change. Keep the archive commit in your repository history if you want Git to retain the deleted files. Squashing the archive and cleanup commits together removes that intermediate snapshot. OpenSpec does not prune archived changes automatically or provide a retention setting. ## [Going further](#going-further) * [Delta specs](/docs/schemas/spec-driven#delta-specs-specmd): how to write the behavior changes in a delta spec. * [Profiles](/docs/profiles): optional workflows beyond the core set (verify before archive, incremental planning). ## [Advanced guides](#advanced-guides) Not written yet; guides we plan to add: * **Prototype first**: spike the code before any spec, then backfill the proposal from what the prototype taught you. * **Building iteratively**: a sequence of small changes instead of one big proposal. * **Revising an implemented change**: the plan needs to move again after apply, but the change hasn't merged or archived yet.

+# Proposal
+
+## Why
+
+The application currently lets either of its approval roles approve any pending invoice in one step. The assignment requires approval authority to reflect invoice value and a distinct Director decision for invoices above 500,000, so a reviewable policy and implementation plan is needed before changing application behavior.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- Add approval limits of 50,000 for Managers and 500,000 for Directors, inclusive.
+- Require two distinct approvers for invoices above 500,000, with the second approver a Director.
+- Define a visible intermediate approval state and preserve the invoice's submitted business data when an approval attempt is denied or an invoice is rejected.
+- Keep authorization, decision recording, API responses, and the approval UI consistent with the new lifecycle.
+- Resolve and record role-mapping, first-approver eligibility, lower-amount eligibility, and storage/concurrency decisions before implementation.
+
+## Capabilities
+
+### New Capabilities
+
+- `invoice-approval-limits`: Role-based amount authority, staged approval for high-value invoices, and rejection/state-integrity behavior.
+
+### Modified Capabilities
+
+None. The repository has no existing OpenSpec capability specs.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Domain behavior and invoice state: `ApprovalService`, `Invoice`, `InvoiceStatus`, and repository update semantics.
+- API [REDACTED] decision endpoints: `ApprovalsController`, existing session roles, and standard service error mapping.
+- Static approval UI: approval queue, progress/state visibility, error display, and role-dependent actions.
+- Unit tests, Playwright E2E tests, mutation-testing tooling/results, AI-assisted PR review, and final documentation.
+
+This proposal is planning-only. It does not authorize application or test changes until the design decisions are reviewed.
*** End Patch

+# Spec Delta
+
+## Purpose
+
+Defines amount-based approval authority and the multi-approver lifecycle for high-value invoices while preserving submitted invoice data and keeping decisions observable.
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Manager approval authority is capped at 50,000
+The system SHALL allow a Manager to approve an invoice of 50,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Manager from approving an invoice above 50,000.
+
+#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000
+- **THEN** the approval is accepted, subject to the approved role mapping and lifecycle policy
+
+#### Scenario: Manager is denied above the limit
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,001
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice state is unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Director approval authority is capped at 500,000
+The system SHALL allow a Director to approve an invoice of 500,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Director from approving an invoice above 500,000 as a single approval.
+
+#### Scenario: Director approves at the inclusive limit
+- **WHEN** a Director attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 500,000
+- **THEN** the approval is accepted, subject to the approved role mapping and lifecycle policy
+
+#### Scenario: A single Director approval cannot approve above the limit
+- **WHEN** a Director attempts to finalize an invoice for 500,001 with only one approval
+- **THEN** the invoice is not finalized and the attempt returns a clear reason
+
+### Requirement: Invoices above 500,000 require two distinct approvals
+An invoice above 500,000 SHALL require two approvals by different users, and the second approval SHALL be made by a Director before the invoice is finalized.
+
+#### Scenario: First approval leaves a high-value invoice non-final
+- **WHEN** an approver eligible under the owner-approved first-approver policy records the first approval for an invoice of 500,001
+- **THEN** the invoice remains in a visible intermediate approval state and is not reported as Approved
+
+#### Scenario: Distinct Director completes the high-value approval
+- **WHEN** a Director different from the first approver records the second approval for an invoice of 500,001
+- **THEN** the invoice moves to Approved and both approval decisions are recorded
+
+#### Scenario: The first user cannot provide the second approval
+- **WHEN** the user who recorded the first approval attempts the second approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the complete invoice state remains unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: A non-Director cannot provide the second approval
+- **WHEN** a user who is not a Director attempts the second approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the complete invoice state remains unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Denied approval attempts do not mutate invoice state
+When an approval attempt is denied by policy or lifecycle validation, the system SHALL return a clear reason and SHALL leave every invoice field unchanged, including its status, submitted data, decision metadata, and recorded approvals.
+
+#### Scenario: Amount-policy denial preserves the invoice
+- **WHEN** an approval attempt exceeds the actor's approved authority
+- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt
+
+#### Scenario: Lifecycle denial preserves the invoice
+- **WHEN** an approval attempt targets an invoice that is not eligible for that approval step
+- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt
+
+### Requirement: Rejection preserves submitted invoice data
+Rejecting an invoice SHALL record the rejection outcome and its decision metadata without changing submitted business data, including the invoice amount and customer details.
+
+#### Scenario: Rejection records outcome without rewriting submitted data
+- **WHEN** an authorized approver rejects a pending invoice with a non-empty reason
+- **THEN** the invoice is Rejected with its actor, decision time, and reason recorded, while its submitted customer details and amount remain unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Approval progress is visible and actionable
+The API and approval UI SHALL distinguish an invoice awaiting its first approval from one awaiting its second approval, show its current progress, and offer only actions permitted by the approved [REDACTED]
+
+#### Scenario: Intermediate invoice appears in the approval queue
+- **WHEN** an invoice has one approval and still requires a Director's second approval
+- **THEN** the API exposes its intermediate state and the UI presents it as awaiting the second approval rather than as Approved or as a new first approval
+
+#### Scenario: A completed invoice is no longer actionable
+- **WHEN** an invoice reaches Approved or Rejected
+- **THEN** the approval UI does not offer another approval or rejection action for that invoice
*** End Patch

# Proposal

The application currently lets either of its approval roles approve any pending invoice in one step. ## What Changes

- Add approval limits of 50,000 for Managers and 500,000 for Directors, inclusive.
- Require two distinct approvers for invoices above 500,000, with the second approver a Director.
- Define a visible intermediate approval state and preserve the invoice's submitted business data when an approval attempt is denied or an invoice is rejected.
- Keep authorization, decision recording, API responses, and the approval UI consistent with the new lifecycle.
- Resolve and record role-mapping, first-approver eligibility, lower-amount eligibility, and storage/concurrency decisions before implementation.

## Capabilities

- `invoice-approval-limits`: Role-based amount authority, staged approval for high-value invoices, and rejection/state-integrity behavior.

*** Add File: openspec/changes/invoice-approval-limits/design.md
+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+The current `ApprovalService` approves or rejects each `PendingApproval` invoice in one step. The invoice has one decision actor/time/note, `InvoiceStatus` has no intermediate approval state, and the singleton in-memory repository returns mutable invoice references. The API authenticates `Approver` and `Admin` sessions and authorizes both for the approval controller; the UI only queues `PendingApproval` invoices. There is no existing OpenSpec capability spec or durable database.
+
+See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval-limits/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval-limits/spec.md) for the externally visible behavior.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+
+- Enforce the approved role limits and require two distinct recorded approvals above 500,000.
+- Make approval progress and denial reasons visible through the API and UI.
+- Ensure denied attempts do not partially mutate an invoice and rejection does not rewrite submitted business data.
+- Keep both implementation stages independently testable and safe to commit.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+
+- Replacing the demo's in-memory repository with a database or adding cross-process persistence.
+- Changing sign-in credentials, [REDACTED], or the existing Admin-only destructive actions without explicit approval.
+- Implementing the feature before the owner reviews this design.
+
+## Decisions
+
+The following are recommendations, not settled product policy. Each item marked **Owner approval required** blocks implementation and policy-dependent tests.
+
+### 1. Map existing roles to business approval roles
+
+**Recommendation — Owner approval required:** Keep the existing session role strings and demo accounts for compatibility, and map `Approver` to the business role `Manager` and `Admin` to `Director` inside the server-side approval boundary. Continue to treat Admin-only destructive permissions separately; being a Director for invoice approval must not broaden unrelated permissions. The UI can display the business-role label while preserving the original session value for authentication.
+
+**Alternatives:** Rename/configure the demo roles as `Manager` and `Director`; or introduce separate approval-role configuration and leave existing app roles without an automatic mapping. Renaming is more disruptive to current sessions, controller attributes, and demo documentation. A separate mapping is more flexible but requires explicit configuration and account ownership decisions.
+
+**Authority below each limit — Owner approval required:** Recommend that a Director's 500,000 ceiling includes invoices at lower amounts, while a Manager is capped at 50,000. The assignment states maxima but does not explicitly say whether Directors may approve invoices at or below 50,000. Confirm this eligibility matrix before tests encode it.
+
+### 2. First approval above 500,000
+
+**Recommendation — Owner approval required:** Permit either mapped business role to record the first concurrence, subject to the owner-approved first-step policy; that first concurrence is not a final approval and does not bypass the two-approver requirement. Require a different Director for the second decision.
+
+**Alternatives:** Require a Director for both steps; permit only a Manager for the first step; or define a separately configured first-approver role. The first option is stricter but requires two Directors, the second is a strong separation-of-duties model but excludes a high-value first decision by a Director, and the third adds configuration surface.
+
+### 3. Model and persist staged approvals
+
+**Recommendation:** Add a distinct intermediate state such as `AwaitingSecondApproval` and store both approval identities/timestamps on the invoice (or in an approval-record collection owned by it). Keep the existing final decision fields meaningful for the completed decision and preserve the original invoice amount/customer data. Use the existing repository as the persistence boundary; in this demo that means approval history survives requests while the process runs but is not durable across restart.
+
+**Alternatives:** Keep `PendingApproval` and infer progress from an approvals count, or store decisions in a separate repository. A separate status makes queue filtering and client behavior explicit; a separate store may be preferable if audit history grows, but it is unnecessary in the current in-memory demo.
+
+**Concurrency:** Serialize each approval transition at the repository/service boundary (for example, an atomic conditional update from the expected status and approval count). Current `GetById` returns a mutable reference and the repository lock does not cover the service's complete read/validate/write sequence; relying on ordinary `Update` calls can allow concurrent requests to act on stale progress. The two-approver stage must prevent duplicate or simultaneous decisions from bypassing the distinct-user check.
+
+### 4. Separate denied attempts from invoice rejection
+
+**Recommendation:** Validate role, amount, lifecycle state, and approver identity before mutating or updating the invoice. Return a specific, user-readable error for a denied approval attempt; use [REDACTED] for a role that is not permitted and a conflict for a valid session whose requested approval step is invalid. The current base controller maps `InvalidOperationException` to HTTP 409, while role filters return 403, so use or extend those established mappings rather than returning success-shaped responses.
+
+An invoice rejection is a recorded business decision: set `Rejected` and decision metadata (actor, time, reason) while leaving submitted fields unchanged. A denied approval attempt is not a business decision and must leave the entire invoice, including decision metadata and approval history, unchanged.
+
+**Alternative:** Treat all policy denials as 403 or all as 409. Choose one API mapping consistently and assert the clear response body in tests. No mapping decision changes the no-mutation guarantee.
+
+### 5. Preserve API and UI compatibility
+
+**Recommendation:** Keep the existing approve/reject endpoints and `PendingApproval` meaning for the first step. Expose a distinct JSON status for the intermediate step, include its approval progress, and make the UI queue both actionable pending states while showing the correct next-step label and business-role eligibility. Completed invoices remain non-actionable.
+
+**Alternative:** Keep one status and add an approval-count field. That minimizes enum changes but makes status filters and client logic less explicit. The repository currently has no external API consumers in the inspected project; if consumers outside this repo exist, confirm their tolerance for a new enum value before implementation.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- **Existing `Admin` is broader than an approval role** → Keep destructive [REDACTED] and test it unchanged; do not equate Director with unrestricted application authority.
+- **The in-memory repository is not durable** → Clearly document restart loss; require a separate approved storage change before promising durable audit retention.
+- **Concurrent approvals can race** → Implement a single atomic transition boundary and test conflicting parallel attempts.
+- **New status values can surprise clients** → Preserve current endpoint behavior, update UI/status filtering, and document the added status.
+- **A high-value first-approver rule may be guessed during implementation** → Treat all owner-approval items above as blockers and do not write policy-dependent tests until answered.
+- **Mutation tooling is not present in the current test project** → Evaluate Stryker.NET as a local test tool; record baseline and post-change mutation results without weakening tests to improve the score.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+1. Owner approves the role mapping, lower-amount eligibility, first-approver rule, intermediate-state representation, and persistence/concurrency scope.
+2. Record a passing test and mutation baseline before implementation.
+3. Implement and test the single-approver limits as one independently passing commit; invoices above 500,000 must remain unapproved at this stage.
+4. Implement and test the second-approval lifecycle as a separate independently passing commit.
+5. Run Playwright E2E coverage, repeat mutation testing, request AI-assisted review of each implementation diff, then update user-facing documentation.
+
+Rollback of the second implementation stage must leave the first-stage guard in place so invoices above 500,000 cannot be finalized by a single approver. Reverting the first stage is a separate decision and must not silently restore unrestricted approvals.
*** End Patch

### 3. Model and persist staged approvals

**Recommendation:** Add a distinct intermediate state such as `AwaitingSecondApproval` and store both approval identities/timestamps on the invoice (or in an approval-record collection owned by it). Keep the existing final decision fields meaningful for the completed decision and preserve the original invoice amount/customer data. Use the existing repository as the persistence boundary; in this demo that means approval history survives requests while the process runs but is not durable across restart.

**Alternatives:** Keep `PendingApproval` and infer progress from an approvals count, or store decisions in a separate repository. A separate status makes queue filtering and client behavior explicit; a separate store may be preferable if audit history grows, but it is unnecessary in the current in-memory demo.

**Concurrency:** Serialize each approval transition at the repository/service boundary (for example, an atomic conditional update from the expected status and approval count). Current `GetById` returns a mutable reference and the repository lock does not cover the service's complete read/validate/write sequence; relying on ordinary `Update` calls can allow concurrent requests to act on stale progress. The two-approver stage must prevent duplicate or simultaneous decisions from bypassing the distinct-user check.

### 4. Separate denied attempts from invoice rejection

**Recommendation:** Validate role, amount, lifecycle state, and approver identity before mutating or updating the invoice. Return a specific, user-readable error for a denied approval attempt; use [REDACTED] for a role that is not permitted and a conflict for a valid session whose requested approval step is invalid. The current base controller maps `InvalidOperationException` to HTTP 409, while role filters return 403, so use or extend those established mappings rather than returning success-shaped responses.

An invoice rejection is a recorded business decision: set `Rejected` and decision metadata (actor, time, reason) while leaving submitted fields unchanged. A denied approval attempt is not a business decision and must leave the entire invoice, including decision metadata and approval history, unchanged.

**Alternative:** Treat all policy denials as 403 or all as 409. Choose one API mapping consistently and assert the clear response body in tests. No mapping decision changes the no-mutation guarantee.

### 5. Preserve API and UI compatibility

**Recommendation:** Keep the existing approve/reject endpoints and `PendingApproval` meaning for the first step. Expose a distinct JSON status for the intermediate step, include its approval progress, and make the UI queue both actionable pending states while showing the correct next-step label and business-role eligibility. Completed invoices remain non-actionable.

**Alternative:** Keep one status and add an approval-count field. That minimizes enum changes but makes status filters and client logic less explicit. The repository currently has no external API consumers in the inspected project; if consumers outside this repo exist, confirm their tolerance for a new enum value before implementation.

- **Existing `Admin` is broader than an approval role** → Keep destructive [REDACTED] and test it unchanged; do not equate Director with unrestricted application authority.
- **The in-memory repository is not durable** → Clearly document restart loss; require a separate approved storage change before promising durable audit retention.
- **Concurrent approvals can race** → Implement a single atomic transition boundary and test conflicting parallel attempts.
- **New status values can surprise clients** → Preserve current endpoint behavior, update UI/status filtering, and document the added status.
- **A high-value first-approver rule may be guessed during implementation** → Treat all owner-approval items above as blockers and do not write policy-dependent tests until answered.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Defines amount-based approval authority and the multi-approver lifecycle for high-value invoices while preserving submitted invoice data and keeping decisions observable.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Manager approval authority is capped at 50,000
The system SHALL allow a Manager to approve an invoice of 50,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Manager from approving an invoice above 50,000.

#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000
- **THEN** the approval is accepted, subject to the approved role mapping and lifecycle policy

#### Scenario: Manager is denied above the limit
- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,001
- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice state is unchanged

### Requirement: Director approval authority is capped at 500,000
The system SHALL allow a Director to approve an invoice of 500,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Director from approving an invoice above 500,000 as a single approval.

#### Scenario: Director approves at the inclusive limit
- **WHEN** a Director attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 500,000
- **THEN** the approval is accepted, subject to the approved role mapping and lifecycle policy

#### Scenario: A single Director approval cannot approve above the limit
- **WHEN** a Director attempts to finalize an invoice for 500,001 with only one approval
- **THEN** the invoice is not finalized and the attempt returns a clear reason

### Requirement: Invoices above 500,000 require two distinct approvals
An invoice above 500,000 SHALL require two approvals by different users, and the second approval SHALL be made by a Director before the invoice is finalized.

#### Scenario: First approval leaves a high-value invoice non-final
- **WHEN** an approver eligible under the owner-approved first-approver policy records the first approval for an invoice of 500,001
- **THEN** the invoice remains in a visible intermediate approval state and is not reported as Approved

#### Scenario: Distinct Director completes the high-value approval
- **WHEN** a Director different from the first approver records the second approval for an invoice of 500,001
- **THEN** the invoice moves to Approved and both approval decisions are recorded

#### Scenario: The first user cannot provide the second approval
- **WHEN** the user who recorded the first approval attempts the second approval
- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the complete invoice state remains unchanged

#### Scenario: A non-Director cannot provide the second approval
- **WHEN** a user who is not a Director attempts the second approval
- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the complete invoice state remains unchanged

### Requirement: Denied approval attempts do not mutate invoice state
When an approval attempt is denied by policy or lifecycle validation, the system SHALL return a clear reason and SHALL leave every invoice field unchanged, including its status, submitted data, decision metadata, and recorded approvals.

#### Scenario: Amount-policy denial preserves the invoice
- **WHEN** an approval attempt exceeds the actor's approved authority
- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt

#### Scenario: Lifecycle denial preserves the invoice
- **WHEN** an approval attempt targets an invoice that is not eligible for that approval step
- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt

### Requirement: Rejection preserves submitted invoice data
Rejecting an invoice SHALL record the rejection outcome and its decision metadata without changing submitted business data, including the invoice amount and customer details.

#### Scenario: Rejection records outcome without rewriting submitted data
- **WHEN** an authorized approver rejects a pending invoice with a non-empty reason
- **THEN** the invoice is Rejected with its actor, decision time, and reason recorded, while its submitted customer details and amount remain unchanged

### Requirement: Approval progress is visible and actionable
The API and approval UI SHALL distinguish an invoice awaiting its first approval from one awaiting its second approval, show its current progress, and offer only actions permitted by the approved [REDACTED]

#### Scenario: Intermediate invoice appears in the approval queue
- **WHEN** an invoice has one approval and still requires a Director's second approval
- **THEN** the API exposes its intermediate state and the UI presents it as awaiting the second approval rather than as Approved or as a new first approval

#### Scenario: A completed invoice is no longer actionable
- **WHEN** an invoice reaches Approved or Rejected
- **THEN** the approval UI does not offer another approval or rejection action for that invoice

# Proposal

## Why

The application currently lets either of its approval roles approve any pending invoice in one step. The assignment requires approval authority to reflect invoice value and a distinct Director decision for invoices above 500,000, so a reviewable policy and implementation plan is needed before changing application behavior.

## What Changes

- Add approval limits of 50,000 for Managers and 500,000 for Directors, inclusive.
- Require two distinct approvers for invoices above 500,000, with the second approver a Director.
- Define a visible intermediate approval state and preserve the invoice's submitted business data when an approval attempt is denied or an invoice is rejected.
- Keep authorization, decision recording, API responses, and the approval UI consistent with the new lifecycle.
- Resolve and record role-mapping, first-approver eligibility, lower-amount eligibility, and storage/concurrency decisions before implementation.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `invoice-approval-limits`: Role-based amount authority, staged approval for high-value invoices, and rejection/state-integrity behavior.

### Modified Capabilities

None. The repository has no existing OpenSpec capability specs.

## Impact

+# Spec Delta
+
+## Purpose
+
+Defines amount-based approval authority and the multi-approver lifecycle for high-value invoices while preserving submitted invoice data and keeping decisions observable.
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Existing roles map to business approval authority only
+For invoice approval only, the system SHALL treat the existing Approver role as Manager and the existing Admin role as Director; this mapping SHALL NOT change administrative or destructive permissions.
+
+#### Scenario: Approver acts as Manager for approval
+- **WHEN** a signed-in user with the existing Approver role attempts an invoice decision
+- **THEN** the system evaluates the user's authority as a Manager without granting administrative permissions
+
+#### Scenario: Admin acts as Director for approval without permission expansion
+- **WHEN** a signed-in user with the existing Admin role attempts an invoice decision
+- **THEN** the system evaluates the user's authority as a Director while preserving the existing scope of Admin-only permissions
+
+### Requirement: Manager approval authority is capped at 50,000
+The system SHALL allow a Manager to approve an invoice of 50,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Manager from approving an invoice above 50,000.
+
+#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000
+- **THEN** the approval is accepted
+
+#### Scenario: Manager is denied above the limit
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,001
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice state is unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Director approval authority is capped at 500,000
+The system SHALL allow a Director to approve an invoice of 500,000 or less, including invoices within the Manager limit, and SHALL prevent a Director from finalizing an invoice above 500,000 with a single approval.
+
+#### Scenario: Director approves within the Manager limit
+- **WHEN** a Director attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000
+- **THEN** the approval is accepted
+
+#### Scenario: Director approves at the inclusive limit
+- **WHEN** a Director attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 500,000
+- **THEN** the approval is accepted
+
+#### Scenario: A single Director approval cannot finalize above the limit
+- **WHEN** a Director attempts to finalize an invoice for 500,001 with only one approval
+- **THEN** the invoice is not finalized and the attempt returns a clear reason
+
+### Requirement: Invoices above 500,000 require two distinct approvals
+An invoice above 500,000 SHALL require two approvals by different users, and the second approval SHALL be made by a Director before the invoice is finalized.
+
+#### Scenario: Either business role provides the first approval
+- **WHEN** a Manager or Director records the first approval for an invoice of 500,001
+- **THEN** the invoice enters AwaitingSecondApproval and is not reported as Approved
+
+#### Scenario: Distinct Director completes the high-value approval
+- **WHEN** a Director different from the first approver records the second approval for an invoice of 500,001
+- **THEN** the invoice moves to Approved and both approval decisions are recorded
+
+#### Scenario: The first user cannot provide the second approval
+- **WHEN** the user who recorded the first approval attempts the second approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and every invoice field, including the first approval, remains unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: A Manager cannot provide the second approval
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts the second approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and every invoice field, including the first approval, remains unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Concurrent approvals preserve approval invariants
+Concurrent approval requests SHALL be serialized so that the invoice cannot be finalized without two distinct approvers or without a Director as the second approver.
+
+#### Scenario: Competing second-approval requests cannot bypass policy
+- **WHEN** concurrent requests attempt to make the second decision on an invoice awaiting second approval
+- **THEN** at most one valid distinct Director decision completes the invoice, and every rejected request leaves the complete state, including prior approvals, unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Denied approval attempts do not mutate invoice state
+When an approval attempt is denied by policy or lifecycle validation, the system SHALL return a clear reason and SHALL leave every invoice field unchanged, including its status, submitted data, decision metadata, and all previously recorded approvals.
+
+#### Scenario: Amount-policy denial preserves the invoice
+- **WHEN** an approval attempt exceeds the actor's approved authority
+- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt
+
+#### Scenario: Lifecycle denial preserves the invoice
+- **WHEN** an approval attempt targets an invoice that is not eligible for that approval step
+- **THEN** the response explains the denial and every field of the invoice equals its value before the attempt
+
+### Requirement: Rejection preserves submitted invoice data
+Rejecting an invoice SHALL record the rejection outcome and its decision metadata without changing submitted business data, including the invoice amount and customer details.
+
+#### Scenario: Rejection records outcome without rewriting submitted data
+- **WHEN** an authorized approver rejects a pending invoice with a non-empty reason
+- **THEN** the invoice is Rejected with its actor, decision time, and reason recorded, while its submitted customer details and amount remain unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Approval progress is visible and actionable
+The API and approval UI SHALL distinguish an invoice awaiting its first approval from an invoice in AwaitingSecondApproval, show its current progress, and offer only actions permitted by the approval authority rules.
+
+#### Scenario: Intermediate invoice appears in the approval queue
+- **WHEN** an invoice has one approval and awaits a different Director's second approval
+- **THEN** the API exposes AwaitingSecondApproval and the UI presents the second-approval step instead of treating it as a new first approval
+
+#### Scenario: A completed invoice is no longer actionable
+- **WHEN** an invoice reaches Approved or Rejected
+- **THEN** the approval UI does not offer another approval or rejection action for that invoice
*** End Patch

+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+The current `ApprovalService` approves or rejects each `PendingApproval` invoice in one step. The invoice has one decision actor/time/note, `InvoiceStatus` has no intermediate approval state, and the singleton in-memory repository returns mutable invoice references. The API authenticates `Approver` and `Admin` sessions and authorizes both for the approval controller; the UI only queues `PendingApproval` invoices. There is no existing OpenSpec capability spec or durable database.
+
+See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval-limits/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval-limits/spec.md) for the externally visible behavior.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+
+- Enforce the approved role limits and require two distinct recorded approvals above 500,000.
+- Make approval progress and denial reasons visible through the API and UI.
+- Ensure denied attempts do not partially mutate an invoice and rejection does not rewrite submitted business data.
+- Keep both implementation stages independently testable and safe to commit.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+
+- Replacing the demo's in-memory repository with a database or adding cross-process persistence.
+- Changing sign-in credentials, [REDACTED], or the existing Admin-only destructive actions.
+- Implementing the feature as part of this planning update.
+
+## Decisions
+
+The following decisions were approved by the human owner on 2026-10-31.
+
+### 1. Map existing roles to business approval roles only
+
+Map the existing `Approver` session role to `Manager` and `Admin` to `Director` only for invoice approval authority. Preserve the existing role strings, sign-in accounts, and Admin-only administrative/destructive permissions.
+

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Defines amount-based approval authority and the multi-approver lifecycle for high-value invoices while preserving submitted invoice data and keeping decisions observable.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Existing roles map to business approval authority only
For invoice approval only, the system SHALL treat the existing Approver role as Manager and the existing Admin role as Director; this mapping SHALL NOT change administrative or destructive permissions.

#### Scenario: Approver acts as Manager for approval
- **WHEN** a signed-in user with the existing Approver role attempts an invoice decision
- **THEN** the system evaluates the user's authority as a Manager without granting administrative permissions

#### Scenario: Admin acts as Director for approval without permission expansion
- **WHEN** a signed-in user with the existing Admin role attempts an invoice decision
- **THEN** the system evaluates the user's authority as a Director while preserving the existing scope of Admin-only permissions

### Requirement: Manager approval authority is capped at 50,000
The system SHALL allow a Manager to approve an invoice of 50,000 or less and SHALL prevent a Manager from approving an invoice above 50,000.

#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000
- **THEN** the approval is accepted

#### Scenario: Manager is denied above the limit
- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,001
- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice state is unchanged

### Requirement: Director approval authority is capped at 500,000
The system SHALL allow a Director to approve an invoice of 500,000 or less, including invoices within the Manager limit, and SHALL prevent a Director from finalizing an invoice above 500,000 with a single approval.

#### Scenario: Director approves within the Manager limit
- **WHEN** a Director attempts to approve an otherwise eligible invoice for 50,000

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Conventions

- Controllers live in `Controllers/`, one per resource, route `api/[controller]`. Request bodies are `record` types declared inside the controller.

- Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
- Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
- Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
- Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
- End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.

- Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
- Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`
